For a heavy subset of size \(k\), all elements must be chosen from \(\{k,k+1,\dots,n\}\), giving
\[
\binom{n-k+1}{k}
\]
choices. This is feasible for \(0\le k\le \lfloor (n+1)/2\rfloor\), with \(k=0\) giving the empty set. Thus
\[
f(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor (n+1)/2\rfloor}\binom{n-k+1}{k}.
\]
For \(n=32\),
\[
f(32)=\sum_{k=0}^{16}\binom{33-k}{k}.
\]
Let
\[
S_n=\sum_{k\ge 0}\binom{n-k+1}{k}.
\]
Using Pascal’s identity,
\[
S_n=S_{n-1}+S_{n-2},
\]
with \(S_0=1,\ S_1=2\), so \(S_n=F_{n+2}\). Therefore
\[
f(32)=S_{32}=F_{34}=5702887.
\]
\[
\boxed{5702887}
\]
